title: Legacy bare DXF TABLE compatibility candidate
mode: Primary-source web research plus local parser/plan cross-check
baselineQualification: The shared worktree was already broadly dirty. Local source and plan observations refer to the shared worktree, not a clean checkout at baselineCommit.
scope: Review a newly screened open-source peer report of bare top-level DXF TABLE records and distinguish compatibility from canonical DXF grammar.
Trace the reported input shape through libdxfrw's section-state parser and existing unknown nested TABLE handling.
Add a conditional, bounded recovery sub-plan without promoting a peer report to a local defect or format-support claim.

method.kind: Current primary-source web review and read-only local source/test/plan inspection
method.limitations: ACadSharp issue #1128 is an open feature request with an asserted legacy NC/CAM/plotter input shape but no inspectable file, producer/version, or reproducible sample. Autodesk's published grammar is canonical; no nonstandard compatibility behavior is inferred to be required. No external file or attachment was downloaded.

sources.observed: The general file structure describes sections beginning with 0/SECTION and 2/<section-name>, ending with 0/ENDSEC, and identifies TABLES as the section containing symbol tables. The symbol-table example places TABLE records inside that section and closes each with ENDTAB. The reported bare top-level TABLE shape is therefore non-canonical under the reviewed documentation.

sources.revision: Open issue body/status reviewed 2026-10-19; no source commit or input artifact supplied in the issue body.
sources.observed: The reporter says some older NC/CAM/plotting exports place TABLE records directly after HEADER without a SECTION/TABLES/ENDSEC wrapper, causing ACadSharp to skip table definitions and leave dependent entities apparently empty. It is a compatibility report/feature request, not a libdxfrw reproduction or canonical grammar rule.

The top-level DXF reader accepts SECTION and EOF framing and returns BAD_READ_SECTION for a record body outside a section. It calls processTables only after reading SECTION/TABLES. processTables handles table records within that canonical section. This is fail-closed behavior; it differs from the silent table skip described for ACadSharp.

sources.revision: Current shared worktree and plan inspection.
sources.observed: PAR-36/7U covers structurally framed unknown nested tables within a valid TABLES section. It does not cover or authorize top-level recovery from a missing TABLES wrapper.

implementationReadiness.conditionalEntryGate: Do not implement recovery until a provenance-eligible representative input or a concrete in-scope consumer need is available; synthetic tests alone can validate a chosen policy but cannot establish the legacy profile's prevalence or intended behavior.
rules: If admitted, recover only a narrowly recognized top-level sequence of known TABLE records; do not accept arbitrary record bodies outside section framing.
Reuse existing table body parsers where feasible and require valid ENDTAB plus sound following section/EOF framing.
Stage table callbacks and publish only after the recovered table sequence is structurally complete; malformed input must not leave partial table state.
Emit a bounded non-fatal diagnostic that labels the input non-canonical and counts/name-limits recovered tables.
Keep unknown bare table names fail-closed until a separate explicit compatibility policy exists.
Serialize recovered semantics through the normal canonical SECTION/TABLES output path; do not preserve the malformed wrapper as if it were standard syntax.
Keep this distinct from PAR-36/7U, which applies only within an existing TABLES section.

If implemented, use generated ASCII and Binary DXF fast controls in the existing parser test target, run only the focused selector and owning CTest, and do not add peer files or a new full-suite cadence.
